Stocks Rally, Shaking Off Fed’s Rate Hike
 
Plus, chip shares soar on Intel CEO comments and SEC clears path for trading tokenized stocks
 
By Heard on the Street Staff
 
 
Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh. GENT SHKULLAKU/ZUMA PRESS
 

This is an edition of the Markets P.M. newsletter, a recap of the day’s most important markets moves, delivered after the closing bell. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here.

 
 
 

What Happened in Markets Today

 

Major stock-market indexes rallied, reversing the declines that followed the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate hike Wednesday. The Nasdaq surged 1.7%, the S&P 500 gained 1.1% and the Dow industrials rose 0.6%. The 10-year Treasury yield declined to 4.946% from just above 5.0% a day earlier. Brent crude fell about 1% to below $105, amid hopes that disruption from a damaged Saudi pipeline may be less severe than initially feared.

 

Chip stocks rallied. The PHLX Semiconductor Index rose 3.1% after comments from Intel Chief Executive Lip-Bu Tan about soaring memory prices. Micron shares jumped 5.5%. Advanced Micro Devices advanced about 6%. Intel’s stock climbed about 8%.

 

The Securities and Exchange Commission cleared a path for trading venues to offer tokenized stocks in the U.S., a landmark decision that may overhaul traditional equity markets. The SEC’s decision came just two days after crypto-related legislation called the Clarity Act failed in the Senate.

 

Generac shares gained 19% after reaching a long-term deal to supply generators to Amazon.com for its data centers. Generac said it expects initial deliveries of backup generators to total $2.4 billion in 2027 and 2028. It also issued a warrant to Amazon to buy shares of its common stock.

 

Mark Walter and Todd Boehly agreed to sell their combined 25% stake in English soccer team Chelsea in a deal that will hand them around $650 million each. Chelsea said they were selling their holdings to Clearlake Capital, the private-equity firm that is already the team’s majority owner. The deal comes as U.S. regulators are probing Walter’s insurance empire, and he has been refinancing assets.
